findings.body: The repository's review rule explicitly requires coverage of an existing client adopted on the previous release. Every upgrade case uses this fixture, which directly syncs a manually configured repo: `tests/test_close.py:228–236` writes its settings using the current checkout's version. The older-pin case only changes that version string; it never adopts a client using the previous release. Add an end-to-end case that adopts and lands the previous release, then runs the upgrade and verifies the resulting files and preserved client settings.
findings.title: Not done: upgrade coverage for a repo adopted on the previous release

findings.body: After close refuses, a user can stage the fix's changes with `git add -A` before rerunning the upgrade. With `core.hooksPath = ".husky/_"`, that also stages sync's new hook shims. `close.synced_changes` at `src/forge/close.py:262` excludes only `??` entries, so staged additions enter `changed` and the commit at line 157 records them. The command therefore commits hook shims it promises to leave out. Exclude newly added hook shims whether they are staged or untracked.
findings.title: Exclude staged new hook shims on an upgrade rerun
